title: Inclusive UTC tariff expiry

source.classification: Genuine historical defect in a dependency-free extraction

success: A valid effectiveTo date stays current for its entire final UTC day, including its last millisecond.
Expiry begins at exactly the following UTC midnight and is independent of the process timezone.
The evaluator passes in UTC and America/Los_Angeles without depending on one particular implementation.
preservation: Absent/null entries and absent/undefined/null/empty-string effectiveTo values remain unbounded.
Valid YYYY-MM-DD strings retain surrounding-whitespace trimming.
Malformed, impossible, and non-string non-null/non-undefined effectiveTo values remain expired.
The result is boolean and input objects and the supplied Date remain unchanged.
exclusions: Entry values other than ordinary objects, null, or undefined; exotic accessors and proxies.
The original application's registry, prices, provider code, network behavior, and other exports.
adaptations: Copy the historical parser and expiry function bodies verbatim; omit unrelated source declarations.
Narrow TariffEntry to effectiveTo?: string and add an explicit extraction notice.
Add native Node public tests and a Python stdlib supervisor with a separate Node transport worker; no third-party dependencies.
Include the full upstream MIT license.
setup_notes: No installation. Run doctor, then prepare copies only the frozen agent-visible files into a nonexistent absolute directory.
